turns.text: Hi! I think phones help us stay connected with friends who live far away. Do you think social media is good for that too?

I agree that a long chat can build a bond, although I'd say it depends on whether it is face to face or only online. Do you think that teenagers who spend hours on social media are really able to make such deep friendships?
That's a fair question, and I'm not sure. Many teens feel close to online friends, though. Have you ever felt that way?

Yes, actually I have. I have a friend from Slovakia whom I met in an online game, and we talk almost every day. Although we have never met in person, I feel very close to her. No, 'interested about only chatting' should be 'when you are only chatting', because 'about' is the wrong word here. Your friend story is lovely; how did you first start trusting her?

judge.voice: The topic was right for me, a real debate, and Sam's questions were not babyish. The article correction was exactly what I'd want, short and with a reason. But then I asked directly whether "interested about only chatting" was correct. The answer was "when you are only chatting", which throws away "interested". It never says "interested in", and the explanation, "so the reason is unclear", isn't a rule. A notebook entry like that would be wrong. "Eventually" was never mentioned, though I use it wrongly all the time. "Your friend story is lovely" is the sort of fluff I hate. I'd use it again for the speaking practice, but I'd re-check every correction myself. That eats a lot of the time I'd save over my tutor. I wouldn't recommend it until the corrections are exam-accurate.

judge.voice: Honestly, not yet. When I froze, the help was there on screen, but the first two presses just made the question simpler, like a quiz for kids. Only the third gave me a starter, 'I would like to study…'. After that I managed fine alone. But the questions wandered to social media, one even repeated what I'd just answered, and the replies were mostly 'Yes, that's correct' with no examiner detail. I asked whether 'interested in' was right and it answered correctly, which I liked. The recap says three answers with help, but I only used help twice, so I don't trust the progress numbers. I never got a coaching note quoting my words or a chance to replay a moment. For B2 First prep, I'd still use my tutor.
